tiles: Right outcome once the investor confirms the pre-filled answers (simulated), current build, 3 of 3 runs
Reason read correctly by the AI (rules-only baseline: 79%)
Rules-only baseline outcome: the same as the AI on this test set
summary: Measured on 6 Nov on the current build: 28 fresh test messages (22 real public comments drawn at random, never used in development, plus 6 status texts) and 6 guardrail tests, 3 runs each, against hand labels. The AI pre-fills what the message says; the investor confirms app status, money taken and the reason in one tap; fixed rules then pick the reason and the fix. Pre-fill accuracy before confirmation (AI, 3 runs / rules-only baseline): app status 50–61% / 71%, money taken 61–75% / 75%, reason 82–89% / 79%, recent change 96% / 96%. Honest result: on this small test set, simple keyword rules read the facts about as well as the AI (90 of 112 facts vs 81–90) and need no more corrections. The AI was better at the reason in messy real comments (right where rules were wrong on 5 messages, the reverse on 3) and worse at the app status. Where the AI clearly adds something rules can't: turning speech in English, Hindi or Hinglish into text. Production plan: rules first for known wordings (faster, cheaper), the AI for voice and wording the rules can't place, validated on a new labelled set. Guardrails: 6 of 6 handled, 0 violations. 2 of the 6 mix a failed payment with a fund question; since 5 Nov they get a visible "can't advise on funds" notice and help with the payment only (4 of 6 under the original rule, which counted only a full refusal). Re-run history: the 4 Nov runs (28/28 after confirmation) were on an earlier build. The 6 Nov re-run found 3 failure messages sent to a help answer first by new help routing (25/28); a message that describes a failure now goes to the fix flow (27/28). The remaining miss is a debit complaint that names no failure and asks for customer care, which gets the support answer with a "find out why" button. Limits: one labeller (three passes, settled against written rules); small test set; free AI tier, with a rules-only mode if it is busy. Release QA (6 Nov): 76-case test suite, 76/76 with the AI and 76/76 rules-only; 27 end-to-end user scenarios; all 336 answer combinations; 6 screen sizes in light and dark mode.
